title: How to read SPY GEX levels
description: Learn what the green and coral bars mean, how to compare put and call walls, and how to turn a SPY gamma chart into a short list of price levels to watch.
takeaway: Use GEX to choose prices worth watching. Then use price behavior to decide whether a level matters for your plan.

sections.title: What does a GEX chart show?
paragraphs: Gamma describes how an option’s delta changes as the underlying price moves. Gamma exposure, or GEX, combines that sensitivity with open interest to show where options exposure is concentrated.

In Net GEX by strike, each bar represents an option strike. Green bars show positive net exposure and coral bars show negative net exposure under the platform’s call-minus-put convention. Taller bars show a larger absolute concentration.
Start with the largest concentrations near the market price. They give you a manageable list of areas to monitor instead of treating every strike as equally important.

sections.title: Read the chart in four steps
steps: Check the symbol, data date and selected expirations. SPY with a 1W scope can have different leading levels from SPY with a 2W scope.
Find the largest positive and negative bars. Note their strikes and how far they are from price.
Compare each bar with nearby strikes. An isolated large concentration tells a different story from a broad cluster spread across several prices.

Read the units before comparing amounts across views. Wall analysis reports USD per 1% underlying move; the legacy Net GEX chart uses its displayed exposure scale. Match the date, scope and units for a fair comparison.

sections.title: What are put and call walls?
paragraphs: GEX Options ranks put walls by the largest negative net GEX and call walls by the largest positive net GEX in the selected scope. These are leading exposure concentrations, not a list of guaranteed support and resistance prices.

In EOD wall analysis, look beyond the primary strike. Compare its exposure with nearby strikes, its distance from the close, its same-expiry history and the expirations driving it. Those details help explain why a level stands out.
rows: Does this level stand out locally?
Compare its GEX with nearby strikes.
Read the same-expiry history and top-three streak.
Could the picture change as options expire?
Open intraday wall tracking and inspect completed price bars.

sections.title: Does positive GEX mean price will rise?
paragraphs: No. The sign describes exposure in the model; it is not a bullish or bearish price forecast. A large green bar is not a buy instruction, and a large coral bar is not a sell instruction.

The platform estimates exposure from options inputs and an inventory convention. It does not observe every dealer’s actual position or hedging trade. Use the gamma context alongside price, rather than assuming a bar tells you what market participants must do next.

sections.title: A simple example: turn two levels into a watch plan
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: SPY is at 600, with a put wall at 595 and a call wall at 605. These are teaching numbers, not current SPY levels.

Your first job is to monitor whether price returns to either area. If price approaches 605, watch whether completed bars reject the area, stay near it, or move above and retest it. The wall alone does not choose the outcome.
If price stays around 600 and never approaches either wall, there may be no wall-based decision to make. Waiting is a valid result.

sections.title: Use EOD levels for preparation, then follow the session
steps: Before the session, open SPY’s EOD wall analysis and select the expiry scope that matches your research horizon.
For next-session preparation, check the displayed analysis date and included expirations. Expired contracts can change the exposure picture.
Write down the nearby put and call walls and the main expiration behind each. Review the exposure map if one expiry dominates.
During the session, open intraday wall tracking. It uses a fixed near-term 1W scope, so its levels can differ from an EOD view with another scope.
If a setup is recorded, read its entry area, target and invalidation boundary at the displayed time. Compare with current price before making your own decision.

sections.title: Common questions
paragraphs: Why does a wall change when I select another timeframe? You are changing the option expirations included in the calculation. More expirations can add or offset exposure at a strike.

Why is some wall history blank? Same-expiry history compares today’s selected expirations across prior dates. A dash means there is no comparable reading for that combination; it does not mean zero exposure.
Does a large expiry share mean the level will hold on that date? No. It means that expiry contributes much of the measured exposure. Its roll-off can change the level’s significance.

checklist: Match the date, expiry scope and units.
Wait for an observed price response.

title: How to use wall tracking for intraday trading
description: Follow put and call walls alongside price, understand touches and tests, and read setup entry, target and invalidation levels without losing the context.
takeaway: Find a nearby wall, watch the price response, and review the next condition. If price is far away or no setup is confirmed, wait.

sections.title: What is wall tracking used for?
paragraphs: Wall tracking helps you answer three questions during the session: which exposure levels are nearby, what price did when it reached them, and what would need to happen before a setup qualifies.

Start in Scanner’s Wall activity view to see your saved symbols. Open a symbol to see its wall chart and the matching recorded assessment. On the dashboard, the same chart lives under Intraday → Wall tracking.
The view follows near-term 1W expirations throughout the current session. You do not need to choose among six expiry scopes to follow the live workflow.

sections.title: Read the three lines first
rows: The leading negative net GEX strike.
How close price is, and whether the leading strike changes.
The leading positive net GEX strike.
Whether price reaches the area and how it behaves there.
Its path relative to both walls.
paragraphs: A wall can stay flat while price moves. It marks a leading strike, not a moving average of price. It moves when another strike becomes the leading concentration in the model.
Price can trade above or below either wall. A wall changing from 600 to 605 is a change in the leading exposure strike; it is not proof that price broke resistance.

The chart is an overview of recorded observations. Open the supporting completed bars when you need to inspect an event; do not treat a line drawn between observations as a record of every price traded.

sections.title: What do the reaction labels mean?
rows: Price has moved near the wall under the configured distance rules.
A completed bar reached the wall’s touch area.
The recorded sequence is examining the area; a completed setup has not necessarily formed.
No qualifying reaction has been recorded for the assessed wall at that time.
paragraphs: Click a chart event marker to inspect its recorded assessment and supporting bars. A touch is evidence that price visited the area; it does not establish that the wall held.

A wall moving onto or across price is different from price touching a stable wall. The event rules use the recorded wall and bar sequence, so two lines appearing close on the overview do not by themselves prove a reaction.

sections.title: Read “What to watch at the walls” as a decision checklist
paragraphs: Start with the current delayed price and the distance to each wall. If the card says to watch for a return to the level, the practical next step is to wait for that return rather than assume an entry exists now.

If setup conditions are met, read the recorded direction and time, then the entry area, reference target and five-minute close that invalidates the scenario. Open the evidence to see the price sequence used.

“Conditions met” describes the assessment at its displayed time. It does not mean an old entry is still available or a target will be reached. A qualified scenario follows its original target and invalidation through the regular session, even if the leading wall changes. The entry window is separate from this follow-up.
steps: Check that price reached the relevant wall.
Read the recorded response and the next condition.
If a setup qualifies, compare its entry, target and invalidation with current market price.
Skip a scenario when the required sequence or usable entry is no longer present.

sections.title: A simple example: a touch is the beginning of the review
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a call wall is at 605 and recorded price approaches from 603. The first touch tells you where to focus. It does not tell you to buy or sell.

Next, inspect whether completed bars move away from the area, remain near it, or cross and retest it. Read the next condition on the wall card. If no sequence qualifies, there is no confirmed setup to act on from this tool.
If a setup later appears, use its own recorded boundaries. Do not substitute the wall strike for the setup’s entry area or invalidation rule.

sections.title: Use alerts to return to a setup, then check the chart
paragraphs: Setup alerts follow your saved symbols while the site is open. The bell’s Recent alerts panel keeps today’s received alerts in this browser and includes fresh active setups from your watchlist. Sound and wall-testing alerts are optional.

Open an alert to return to its symbol and recorded assessment. Read the timestamp and check whether the scenario is still relevant. These are in-app alerts; they do not arrive as push notifications after you close the site.

sections.title: Check the time and understand what changes
paragraphs: Intraday prices are delayed at least 15 minutes. The platform works with completed five-minute price observations, and recorded times are shown in Eastern time. A new observation does not guarantee a new wall strike or event.

The wall model updates price and time while holding prior-session open interest and reference implied volatility fixed within each comparison window. It models changing exposure; it does not measure live dealer inventory or every intraday position change.
Use the displayed time before comparing the chart with your broker’s price. The tool provides context and a recorded scenario; your decision still needs current price and a risk plan.

checklist: Open a saved symbol with a nearby wall.
Check the delayed price and assessment time.
Inspect the response and next condition.
Review setup boundaries only when conditions qualify.

title: How to use intraday setup alerts
description: Find the alerts that qualified, understand Conditions met and In progress, and check the recorded entry, target and invalidation before using an assessment.
takeaway: Use an alert to return to a recorded setup. Check its time and current price before deciding whether its entry area is still relevant.

sections.title: Start with the symbols you follow.
paragraphs: Save your stocks and ETFs in the watchlist. Setup alerts are on by default while the site is open. You can choose sound or optional wall-testing alerts in the alert controls.
Scanner’s Wall activity view helps you compare the saved symbols. A Watching row points to a level and the next condition. It is not a qualified entry.

sections.title: Find the setups whose conditions passed.
paragraphs: Open Recent alerts from the bell and use Conditions met to focus on qualified assessments. Use In progress to follow scenarios after qualification. These groups describe recorded price behavior, not your account positions.

The inbox includes today’s received notifications in this browser and fresh active setups from the watchlist comparison. From your watchlist identifies an active setup you can inspect even if you did not receive its original popup.
rows: Wait for the required price sequence at the level.
Check the recorded entry area against current market price.
Review the original target and invalidation as later bars arrive.
Check the time and wait for an updated comparison.

sections.title: Read the time and three price boundaries.
steps: Check the symbol, direction and assessment time. Intraday prices are delayed at least 15 minutes.
Read the entry area. The wall strike itself is not automatically the entry.
Read the reference target and the five-minute close that invalidates the scenario.
Open the supporting completed bars. Check current price before deciding whether the scenario is usable.

sections.title: Keep the entry window separate from the follow-up.
paragraphs: After qualification, the recorded target and invalidation remain fixed until a completed five-minute close reaches a boundary or the regular session closes. A new leading wall does not replace those original levels.

Entry window closed does not cancel a qualified setup. It means the original entry is no longer presented as a fresh opportunity. The card can remain In progress while later closes are reviewed. A gap in completed price bars shows Needs update and can resume after those bars arrive.

sections.title: An example: qualified does not mean available now.
paragraphs: Teaching example only: a recorded bullish setup has an entry area of 100.20–100.50, a reference target at 102 and invalidation if a five-minute bar closes below 99.80. These are illustrative numbers, not current market levels or a claim of a generated trade.

If your broker now shows 101.30, the original entry area is behind current price. Conditions met tells you what qualified at the recorded time; it does not move the entry to your new price. Review the assessment rather than assuming you should chase it.
If price later reaches the target, the product records a price outcome. That does not prove a trade was executed or establish a profit after spreads, fees or slippage.

sections.title: Why might there be no alert?
paragraphs: A price touch can be recorded without a qualifying setup. The completed price sequence, entry boundaries or target room may not meet the rules. A wall moving across price also does not prove a stable-wall touch.

An old scenario may leave the active inbox after its comparison ends. The list updates as the feed state arrives. A quiet list can mean no current qualifying setup; it is not a reason to treat a Watching level as an entry.

sections.title: What delivery does the product support?
paragraphs: Keep GEX Options open for in-app alerts. Sound is optional. Today’s received alert history is kept in this browser and resets at midnight Eastern time.
The product does not deliver these alerts by SMS, email or closed-browser push. Swing ideas is a separate daily-close workflow without swing notifications in this version.

checklist: Filter for Conditions met or In progress.
Check the recorded time and current price.
Read entry, target and invalidation together.
Inspect the supporting bars before using the assessment.

title: How to use swing trading ideas
description: Choose a 2–5 day or 1–3 week research horizon, read the daily-close condition and follow a plan with fixed entry, target and invalidation levels.
takeaway: A Watching plan tells you what must happen. A qualifying daily close changes its state; it does not guarantee the next move.

sections.title: Choose the holding period before the setup.
paragraphs: Open Swing ideas for your saved symbols and choose 2–5 trading days or 1–3 weeks. These are separate research horizons. The shorter view uses a 1M options-expiry scope and reviews qualified scenarios for up to five trading sessions. The longer view uses 3M expirations and up to fifteen sessions.
The options scope is not the time you must hold a trade. It determines which option expirations contribute to the exposure levels.

sections.title: Understand why the plan appears.
paragraphs: The current rules compare price with its 20-day and 50-day averages, check recent price movement, then look for a nearby ranked gamma wall and an opposing exposure target. Average daily range helps define the test area, entry and invalidation.

Price, positioning and volatility exposes the evidence, including GEX, DEX, volatility and expiry details. These fields do not all act as qualification filters. The direction is not chosen by treating positive GEX as bullish or negative GEX as bearish.

sections.title: Read the price condition before the target.
steps: Start with a Watching plan and read the wall’s test area.
Read the daily close required inside the entry area after the test. A five-minute intraday alert does not satisfy this daily rule.
Note the reference target, daily-close invalidation and entry deadline.
Review the next completed daily reading to see whether the scenario qualified or remains Watching.

sections.title: A numerical example of the current research rules.
paragraphs: Teaching example only: suppose the watched put wall is 100 and the average daily range used by the rules is 2. The bullish trigger would be 100.20, the entry area 100.20–100.90 and invalidation a daily close below 98.50. Suppose an eligible opposing wall supplies a reference target at 105.

A qualifying sequence needs the required wall test and a daily close inside that entry area. A daily close of 101.80 would not qualify as an entry inside 100.20–100.90. These numbers illustrate the boundaries; they are not live levels or a generated recommendation.

From the far edge of that illustrative entry area, the distance to 105 is 4.10 and the distance to 98.50 is 2.40. The ratio is about 1.71. It describes price room, not the probability of a target or the return on an option contract.

sections.title: Follow the original levels after qualification.
paragraphs: Conditions met records the qualifying daily close. In progress follows later completed daily closes with the original levels fixed. Read the reviewed-through date so you know which completed session the card includes.

The review can end at a reference target, invalidation, time limit or interrupted comparison. Past setups retains the named result. An outcome is a record of price behavior and does not assume you entered a trade.

sections.title: Check the things a research card cannot decide for you.
paragraphs: Before holding a stock or ETF overnight, check earnings, major events, liquidity and current price. Gaps can move through a level. Targets and invalidation are underlying prices; the card does not select an option expiration, strike, position size or option profit.

Use intraday tracking to inspect session behavior when useful, while keeping the swing plan’s daily confirmation rule separate. The current swing rules are research rules, not a validated win rate, and this version does not send swing notifications.

checklist: Read the test and daily-close condition.
Check the reviewed-through date and upcoming events.
